rhs_question_text:
A small animation studio is upgrading its computers. Its processor communicates through three kinds of bus.

State the distinct purpose of the data bus, address bus and control bus. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Data bus: transfers data or instructions between computer components. Address bus: carries the location of a memory address being accessed. Control bus: carries control or coordination signals.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Award one mark per correctly described bus, up to three. Do not credit a function assigned to the wrong bus.
rhs_marking_guidance_draft: Data bus transfers data or instructions; address bus carries a memory location; control bus carries coordinating signals.

rhs_question_text:
A team is building a history-themed computer game for a museum. It must draw graphics, create sounds and test the game on a computer.

Name one suitable input device and one suitable output device. For each device, explain a specific way the team could use it during development. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Possible input: graphics tablet for drawing game characters; keyboard for entering test commands; microphone for recording narration; mouse for editing artwork. Possible output: monitor for inspecting visuals; speakers for listening to audio. Other sensible game-development examples are acceptable.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Input device 1; contextual input use 1; output device 1; contextual output use 1. The claimed use must fit the named device and game-development setting.
rhs_marking_guidance_draft: Name a suitable input device and explain its use in the game-design task; name a suitable output device and explain a use in designing, editing or testing the game.

rhs_question_text:
A museum game designer needs somewhere to keep many large image, audio and high-definition video files.

Recommend one type of secondary storage and explain one reason that makes it appropriate. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Solid-state storage is acceptable for robust construction, capacity or quick reads/writes; magnetic storage is acceptable for capacity and cost per unit or suitably fast access.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for solid-state or magnetic storage, one for a suitable reason linked to that type. Do not credit optical storage for this reference-linked task.
rhs_marking_guidance_draft: One acceptable storage choice is solid state, linked to robustness or fast access; another is magnetic, linked to capacity or lower cost per unit.

rhs_question_text:
A computer for a new 3D educational game has both a CPU and a GPU.

Choose the more suitable processor, CPU or GPU, for each workload:
• Running thousands of similar straightforward calculations concurrently on a very large set of pixels.
• Performing a smaller number of differing, complicated operations on a limited dataset. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Large-scale parallel simple operations: GPU. Smaller set of complex operations: CPU.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each correctly classified workload, maximum two; do not credit contradictory classifications.

rhs_question_text:
During testing, a development team uses a GPU to draw the graphics in its computer game.

State two different benefits that this could bring to the visual experience of the player. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Any two distinct graphical benefits, such as smoother frame rates, more detailed or realistic visuals, higher image resolution or shorter rendering delays.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each distinct benefit directly connected to rendering or displaying game graphics; up to two. Generic statements about the number of GPU cores are insufficient.

rhs_question_text:
A student routinely has a code editor, web browser and image editor running at once on one computer.

Identify the type of operating system needed to manage these applications simultaneously. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: A multitasking operating system.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for multitasking.

rhs_question_text:
A desktop operating system uses a multi-level feedback queue to schedule its active processes.

Describe three features of how this scheduling method manages processes. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Processes occupy different priority queues. Different queues may use different time slices or scheduling rules. Processes can change queues according to their behaviour or priority; the scheduler balances responsive and longer-running work.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each distinct accurate scheduling feature, maximum three. Avoid granting several marks for repeated descriptions of priority.

rhs_question_text:
A school purchases a new graphics tablet, but its operating system cannot use all the tablet features until additional software is installed.

Explain why a hardware device may need a device driver. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: A driver provides the interface between the operating system/applications and the specific hardware. It translates or interprets software commands into device-specific operations, hiding hardware details.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Award two distinct relevant points showing interface/communication and device-specific instruction translation or compatibility; maximum two.

rhs_question_text:
A school technician is preparing new laptops for pupils.

Name two different utility programs that could be installed and state one purpose of each. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Examples: backup copies files for recovery; antivirus detects/protects against malware; compression reduces storage required; encryption makes stored information unreadable without the right key; disk cleanup removes unnecessary files; file repair restores damaged files.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: For each of two different utilities: one mark for the named utility and one for its valid purpose. Four marks maximum; avoid counting the same utility twice.

rhs_question_text:
An engineering company is choosing a processor architecture for computers that run control-system simulations.

Compare the Von Neumann and Harvard architectures using two different architectural features. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Von Neumann shares memory for instructions and data whereas Harvard separates them. Von Neumann uses a shared bus/path for these whereas Harvard uses separate paths. Harvard can fetch instructions and data simultaneously; Von Neumann commonly shares access.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Two fully paired comparisons of different architectural features. Two marks per comparison when both systems are correctly contrasted; four total.

rhs_question_text:
A processor designer proposes dividing instruction processing into overlapping stages.

State two specific performance benefits that pipelining may provide. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Higher instruction throughput, overlapping work from multiple instruction stages and fewer idle stages / better hardware utilisation.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each distinct valid benefit, maximum two. Unsupported wording such as 'it becomes faster' is insufficient.

rhs_question_text:
A robotics company is evaluating a RISC processor against a CISC processor.

Compare two different technical characteristics of these approaches. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Examples of paired contrasts: RISC has a smaller/simple instruction set versus the larger/complex CISC set; RISC instructions commonly need fewer cycles versus complex CISC instructions that may use more; RISC may be easier to pipeline whereas CISC may be harder; RISC hardware tends to be less complex.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Award two marks per full, same-feature RISC-versus-CISC comparison; maximum four. Listing unrelated statements without a matched contrast does not earn full comparison credit.

rhs_question_text:
A film-rendering workstation is being upgraded from one processor core to a multicore processor.

Describe one advantage of using several cores rather than only one. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Independent instructions or threads can be handled concurrently by separate cores, enabling parallel work or improved responsiveness/throughput when workloads can use it.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for a valid concurrent-processing feature and one for the resulting practical benefit or development; maximum two.

rhs_question_text:
A conservation charity has scientists working from home and field offices. They query large datasets that include confidential information. The charity is comparing two designs:
• Thin client: user machines mainly collect input and show results; virtual machines on a central server do the main processing, and storage is presented virtually.
• Thick client: most processing runs on researchers' own computers, using specialist software that accesses central data.

Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both approaches. Explain virtual machines and virtual storage, consider security, network reliability, performance and cost, and justify which approach would be most appropriate for this charity. [9]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Discuss that a virtual machine is a software-defined computing environment running on physical hardware; virtual storage presents centrally/remote-held data as usable storage. Thin clients can simplify central security and maintenance, share/scalably allocate processing, and reduce endpoint requirements, but depend on reliable bandwidth and remote services. Thick clients can use local processing and may offer some offline capability, but require stronger endpoints, patching and greater local security effort. A valid conclusion weighs the charity's remote/field connectivity, confidentiality and intensive queries.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Use the nine-mark OCR levels-of-response approach, not nine isolated ticks. Consider accurate definitions, application to this specific charity, balanced benefits/drawbacks and a justified conclusion. Indicative bands: 1–3 basic; 4–6 sound; 7–9 thorough and well-justified. Teacher assessment required.

rhs_question_text:
A studio's computer stores the denary identifier 189.

Write 189 as an eight-bit binary value. [1]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for the correct eight-bit binary representation.

rhs_question_text:
The same studio assigns a file the denary identifier 189.

Convert 189 into hexadecimal. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: BD
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for BD.

rhs_question_text:
An embedded controller records the hexadecimal value E4.

Convert E4 into denary. [1]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for 228.

rhs_question_text:
A sensor records a positive integer in binary. The processor shifts all its bits three places to the right.

Explain the arithmetic effect of this shift on the value. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Right-shifting three positions corresponds to dividing the original positive integer value by 2³, which is 8 (with low-order bits lost for a fixed-width integer).
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Award one mark for division/scaling down and one for the factor of eight (or 2³).

rhs_question_text:
An astronomy program stores normalised binary floating-point values using a signed six-bit mantissa and a signed four-bit exponent.

Calculate the following subtraction in the same representation, showing alignment and binary working:

011010 0011 − 010010 0010

Give the final six-bit mantissa and four-bit exponent. [6]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Exponent values are 3 and 2. Align the mantissas to a common exponent, carry out the subtraction in binary, then store the result as mantissa 010001 and exponent 0011.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Six source-linked marks across conversion/alignment of exponents and mantissas, valid binary subtraction and correct final mantissa (010001) and exponent (0011). Follow the specific OCR scheme for part-credit and valid alternative working; do not award the binary-working mark for an entirely denary calculation.

rhs_question_text:
A device checks individual bits using a bitwise AND operation.

Calculate the eight-bit result of:

1010 0011
AND 1010 1110

Show the result as two four-bit groups. [2]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for the correct high nibble 1010 and one for the correct low nibble 0010.

rhs_question_text:
A program applies an AND mask to a stored eight-bit value.

State one reason that a program would use this kind of bit mask. [1]
rhs_answer_points_draft: To retain, test or clear selected bit positions in a stored value, or to extract required bits.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for a valid purpose, such as isolating selected bits or enabling/disabling particular bits.

rhs_question_text:
A community coding club learns Little Man Computer (LMC). Give the mnemonic for each action, in order:
1. Read a value from a named memory location into the accumulator.
2. Branch to an instruction unconditionally.
3. Copy the accumulator into a named memory location.
4. Branch only when the accumulator is zero.
5. Branch if the accumulator is zero or positive. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: 1 LDA; 2 BRA; 3 STA; 4 BRZ; 5 BRP. Accept valid specification synonyms such as LOAD, BR, STO, BZ, BP.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Apply the unusual original scoring: 1 correct match earns 1 mark; 2–4 correct matches earn 2; all 5 correct earn 3. Correctness is positional.

rhs_question_text: At a robotics competition, a console accepts two different non-negative scores. Write an LMC program that reads them both and outputs the larger score. Include any DAT storage locations and valid labels. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft:
One valid solution:
INP
STA FIRST
INP
STA SECOND
LDA FIRST
SUB SECOND
BRP FIRST_WINS
LDA SECOND
OUT
HLT
FIRST_WINS LDA FIRST
OUT
HLT
FIRST DAT 0
SECOND DAT 0
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Four independent marks: both inputs and valid storage; subtraction comparing the values; appropriate conditional branch; correct larger-value output for both paths. Accept correct alternate LMC code and approved mnemonics.

rhs_question_text:
A community technology organisation has five projects: (1) a mobile app showing local news; (2) an embedded river-level sensor transmitting readings; (3) a desktop poster-editing application; (4) scientific analysis of terabytes of environmental measurements; (5) a device driver for a new scanner.

Discuss suitable uses of high-level and low-level languages for these projects. Explain what distinguishes the two language types, consider their advantages and limitations, and reach a justified conclusion about the need for both. [12]
rhs_answer_points_draft: High-level languages generally aid readability, speed of development, debugging, portability and reusable libraries, suiting apps and rich desktop tools. Lower-level approaches offer control over hardware, memory and instruction behaviour, relevant to drivers and embedded systems. Large-scale analysis may use either high-level scientific libraries or optimised low-level routines. Compare trade-offs and justify individual project choices.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Use holistic 12-mark levels of response, not 12 isolated ticks: low 1–4, sound 5–8, thorough 9–12. Strong answers apply knowledge to the five situations, balance arguments and give a justified conclusion. Teacher marking is required.

rhs_question_text:
A binary arithmetic component adds single-bit signals A and B. It sends A XOR B to the sum output S, and A AND B to the carry output C.

Complete the output cells for the four input pairs below. [4]
A | B | S | C
0 | 0 | ? | ?
0 | 1 | ? | ?
1 | 0 | ? | ?
1 | 1 | ? | ?
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each complete correct S,C row, maximum four.

rhs_question_text: A computing student has built one half-adder and one full-adder. Describe two differences between the inputs that these two kinds of adder can process. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Half-adder takes two individual binary inputs with no incoming carry. Full-adder has a third input for carry from an earlier stage.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for the half-adder's two-bit/no-carry-in limitation; one for the full-adder's third carry-in bit.

rhs_question_text:
A team has begun a full-adder circuit for one-bit inputs A, B and Cin. Two existing gates already receive A and B: an XOR and an AND. The completed circuit needs a Sum output S and a Carry output Cout.

Draw the additional logic gates and connections necessary to complete the circuit, showing the two outputs. Use no unnecessary gates. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Let X=A XOR B and C1=A AND B. Connect X and Cin into another XOR to make S; connect X and Cin into another AND to make C2; combine C1 and C2 with OR to make Cout.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for the second XOR with X,Cin; one for the second AND with X,Cin; one for the OR of the two carry signals; one for both outputs correctly connected without unnecessary gates.

rhs_question_text:
A four-input smart-light controller produces F from binary inputs A, B, C and D. Below is an independently arranged Karnaugh map: AB labels the rows, CD labels the columns, and both use Gray-code order.

AB / CD | 00 | 01 | 11 | 10
00 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0
01 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0
11 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1
10 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1

Identify valid groups of adjacent 1s, including wrap-around if appropriate. Write the minimum sum-of-products expression for F, showing the groups used. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: F = (A AND NOT D) OR (B AND NOT C). There are two four-cell groups, one with A=1,D=0 and the other with B=1,C=0; wrapping and overlap are allowed.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for both correct implicant groups; one for A AND NOT D; one for B AND NOT C; one for the OR combination, maximum four.

rhs_question_text: A company creating audio and video editing software uses existing programming libraries instead of developing all features itself. Explain four distinct benefits for the developers. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Faster development/debugging; access to already-tested routines; potentially optimised performance; lower knowledge requirements for complex routines; cross-platform reuse; consistency across software; reduced distributed size where shared modules are used.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per different specific development benefit, maximum four; an unsupported 'saves time' is insufficient.

rhs_question_text:
A programming class labels compiler stages as follows: A lexical analysis, B syntax analysis, C code generation, D code optimisation.

For each description write the correct letter:
1. Produce instructions in a lower-level form.
2. Improve performance without changing what the program does.
3. Remove non-essential characters and form tokens.
4. Check syntax and build a representation of the code's structure. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: C, D, A, B, respectively.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per correctly matched letter, maximum four.

rhs_question_text: During development of a classroom application, a programmer tests code using an interpreter. State two distinct benefits compared with compiling an entire program first. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Faster incremental testing; simpler line-by-line debugging; errors reported at the offending statement; code may be run on other architectures with a compatible interpreter.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each distinct interpreter benefit, up to two.

rhs_question_text: A media company distributes an executable built with a compiler. State two distinct benefits of compiling software before distribution. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: No need to give customers source code; potentially faster execution; optimisation; no matching run-time interpreter required; distribution of executable output.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct valid advantage, maximum two.

rhs_question_text:
A school media club stores software products in TblSoftware(ProductID, Name, Type, Price), where Price is a number in pounds. The table currently contains:
ProductID | Name | Type | Price
EDU01 | EDUCanvas | Image | 129.99
EDU02 | EDUDraw | Image | 119.99
EDU03 | EDUAnimate | Image | 99.99
EDU04 | EDUMovie | Video | 189.99
EDU05 | EDUEffects | Video | 99.99
EDU06 | EDUAudio | Sound | 119.99

The club now licenses a sound program with ProductID EDU07, Name EDUCast, Type Sound and Price 89.99. Write one complete SQL INSERT statement that adds this record. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft:
INSERT INTO TblSoftware (ProductID, Name, Type, Price)
VALUES ('EDU07', 'EDUCast', 'Sound', 89.99);
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Mark the correct INSERT INTO/table and fields; VALUES clause; and correctly ordered values, up to three. Full marks require correct working SQL. These RHS names differ from OCR identifiers.

rhs_question_text:
A school media club stores software products in TblSoftware(ProductID, Name, Type, Price), where Price is a number in pounds. The table currently contains:
ProductID | Name | Type | Price
EDU01 | EDUCanvas | Image | 129.99
EDU02 | EDUDraw | Image | 119.99
EDU03 | EDUAnimate | Image | 99.99
EDU04 | EDUMovie | Video | 189.99
EDU05 | EDUEffects | Video | 99.99
EDU06 | EDUAudio | Sound | 119.99

Write an SQL statement using a nested SELECT to return Name for software costing less than EDUDraw. The threshold must come from a subquery, not a fixed number. [5]
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Five source-aligned criteria: SELECT Name FROM TblSoftware; WHERE Price <; inner SELECT Price; inner FROM TblSoftware; inner WHERE Name = 'EDUDraw'. Equivalent correctly nested syntax accepted.

rhs_question_text:
A free creative-arts website generates images from text descriptions using an AI system. Its developers propose training the system with millions of scraped online photographs, including people and private property.

Discuss the legal and moral implications of this approach. Explain AI, consider consent, ownership, privacy, diversity and fairness, and recommend whether and how the developers should proceed. [9]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Describe AI as software carrying out tasks involving intelligent-seeming decisions or learned patterns. Evaluate personal-data/privacy obligations, informed consent, intellectual-property/licensing, legitimate access to photographs, representation/bias and safeguards. Conclude with a justified position, such as properly licensed and consented diverse training data rather than uncontrolled scraping.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Nine-mark holistic level response: basic 1–3, sound applied 4–6, detailed/balanced/justified 7–9, none 0. Treat named laws carefully; teaching notes are not legal determinations. Human marking required.

rhs_question_text:
An animation club compresses four rows of a nine-pixel-wide monochrome design. W means white, B means black, and the following number gives the run length.

Decode each row into nine pixels in a four-row grid. Shade black cells or write W/B. [4]
Row 1: W4 B1 W4
Row 2: W3 B3 W3
Row 3: W2 B5 W2
Row 4: W1 B7 W1
rhs_answer_points_draft:
Nine cells per row:
WWWWBWWWW
WWWBBBWWW
WWBBBBBWW
WBBBBBBBW
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per complete correct row, up to four.

rhs_question_text: A sports club stores member details, quiz topics, questions and results in one large flat-file database. Explain four distinct problems this design could cause as the club grows. [4]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Duplicate or redundant data; inconsistency/update anomalies; larger storage; less efficient searches; difficult maintenance; poor extension to new relationships; limitations with integrity/transactions.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark per distinct valid limitation, maximum four.

rhs_question_text:
A learning centre is designing four quiz database tables:
TblLearner(LearnerID PK, LearnerName)
TblTopic(TopicID PK, TopicName)
TblTest(TestID PK, TopicID FK, TestTitle)
TblAttempt(AttemptID PK, LearnerID FK, TestID FK, Score)

Draw an entity relationship diagram linking all four tables with the correct one-to-many connectors. Do not add any relationships not implied by the keys. [3]
rhs_answer_points_draft: TblLearner (one) to TblAttempt (many); TblTest (one) to TblAttempt (many); TblTopic (one) to TblTest (many).
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each correct relationship, maximum three; additional incorrect edges prevent full credit. Render with appropriate one-to-many graphical notation rather than only descriptive words.

rhs_question_text: A relational table has a composite primary key. State two requirements for it to satisfy Second Normal Form. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Already in First Normal Form; each non-key attribute depends on the complete key (no partial key dependency).
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for 1NF and one for absence of partial dependency.

rhs_question_text: A table is being converted to Third Normal Form. State two requirements that must be met. [2]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Already in Second Normal Form; no transitive dependency between non-key attributes (non-key attribute depends only on key).
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for 2NF and one for no non-key-to-non-key dependency.

rhs_answer_points_draft: Blanks in order: answers; score; qCount; score + 1; return.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: One mark for each correct blank at its correct location, maximum five. No additional hidden scoring conditions.
